# Test USB boot priority control via Controller API and LPS
# This test verifies that boot order can be controlled:
#   1. Via Controller API: VmConfig.boot_order field in AppInstanceConfig
#   2. Via LPS: /api/v1/appbootinfo endpoint with bootOrderConfig
#
# PREREQUISITES:
# ==============
# This test requires:
# 1. An EVE image with patched OVMF that reads fw_cfg for boot order control
#    (e.g., from the feature/usb-boot-order-config branch in eve repo)
# 2. A USB disk image (Debian) attached to EVE's QEMU
#
# Before running this test, follow these steps:
#
# Step 1: Clean and build Eden
#   make clean
#   rm -rf ~/.eden
#   make build-tests
#
# Step 2: Run the USB boot setup script
#   EVE_TAG="<tag-with-patched-ovmf>" ./tests/eclient/usb-boot-setup.sh
#   # Example: EVE_TAG="0.0.0-feature_usb-boot-order-config-c85715b2-dirty-2025-12-23.13.23" ./tests/eclient/usb-boot-setup.sh
#
# Step 3: Run Eden setup
#   ./eden setup
#
# Step 4: Configure port forwarding (AFTER setup)
#   ./dist/bin/eden+ports.sh 8027:8027 8028:8028 8029:8029 8030:8030 8031:8031
#
# Step 5: Start Eden and onboard EVE
#   ./eden start
#   ./eden eve onboard
#
# Step 6: Run
#   ./eden test tests/eclient -v debug -e usb_boot_priority
#
# What this test verifies:
# The fw_cfg "opt/eve.bootorder" tells OVMF (UEFI firmware) how to order boot devices.
# - "usb": Prioritize USB devices in boot order -> VM boots from USB disk (Debian)
# - "nousb": Deprioritize USB devices in boot order -> VM boots from main drive (Ubuntu)
# - "" or unset: Default boot order (determined by FML resolution config)
#
# TEST ORGANIZATION (Simple to Complex):
# ======================================
#
# PHASE 1: NO LPS REQUIRED (Controller API and Device Property)
# These tests run first, before LPS is deployed.
#   TC-DEV-1 to TC-DEV-3: Device property app.boot.order tests
#   TC-CTRL-1 to TC-CTRL-4: Controller API boot_order tests
#   TC-PRIO-1: Device vs Controller priority (no LPS)
#   TC-EMPTY-1: Empty string at Controller level
#
# PHASE 2: LPS REQUIRED (LPS endpoint tests)
# LPS (local-manager) is deployed, then these tests run.
#   TC-INSTALL-1: *** MAIN CUSTOMER USE CASE ***
#                 OS installation workflow from USB in FML mode
#                 Deploys 3 apps (2 FML VMs + 1 container) like typical customer
#                 (Device=nousb default -> LPS=usb install -> LPS=UNSPECIFIED post-install)
#   TC-PRIO-2: Full priority hierarchy with LPS (LPS > Controller > Device)
#   TC-PRIO-4: LPS clear -> fallback to Controller (tests cache clearing)
#   TC-PRIO-3: Device property as fallback when Controller/LPS empty
#   TC-PRIO-5: LPS explicit UNSPECIFIED -> fallback to Device (different code path)
#   TC-EMPTY-2 to TC-EMPTY-8: LPS edge cases (empty values, 404, etc.)
#   TC1-TC6: Basic LPS boot order tests
#   TC7: Multi-VM with different LPS settings
#   TC8-TC9: LPS config parsing (UUID/displayname)
#   TC10: LPS address change handling
#   TC11-TC13: HTTP status codes (200, 204, 404)
#   TC14-TC16: Config reset methods
#
# PHASE 3: EVE REBOOT REQUIRED (Persistence tests - most complex)
# These tests trigger EVE reboots to verify persistence.
#   TC17: Basic LPS config persistence across EVE reboot
#   TC17-HIER: Full hierarchy persistence (LPS > Controller > Device)
#   TC18: Warning when setting boot order on running VM
#
# LPS Persistence Behavior:
#   Since LPS runs as a VM on the same EVE device, it's unavailable during EVE
#   reboot until the LPS VM starts. EVE persists LPS boot configs to disk so
#   they can be applied immediately when VMs start, before LPS is available.
#
#   - LPS unavailable (during EVE boot): Cache preserved, persisted config applied
#   - HTTP 404: Cache CLEARED (LPS has no config → fall back to Controller/Device)
#   - HTTP 204: Cache preserved (no changes)
#   - HTTP 200 with apps: Cache updated (apps not in list are reset to default)
#   - HTTP 200 with empty list: Cache cleared (ALL apps reset to default)
#
#   KEY: LPS unavailable PRESERVES cache; 404 CLEARS cache.
#
# The USB disk contains Debian, the main drive contains Ubuntu cloud image.
# We verify the correct OS booted by checking console output for "Debian" vs "Ubuntu".
#
# KNOWN LIMITATION: When Debian boots from USB, the VM may crash shortly after boot
# because EVE's usbmanager may disconnect the USB device. The test uses polling
# to catch the brief RUNNING state and verify boot OS from console logs.
#
# NOTE: The USB disk (Debian) is attached via --adapters USB<bus>:<port> passthrough.
# The usb_boot field in LPS API accepts enum values: BOOT_ORDER_UNSPECIFIED, BOOT_ORDER_USB, BOOT_ORDER_NOUSB
# The boot_order field in Controller API (VmConfig) accepts enum values: BOOT_ORDER_UNSPECIFIED, BOOT_ORDER_USB, BOOT_ORDER_NOUSB
# The app.boot.order device property accepts strings: "", "usb", "nousb"
# LPS takes precedence over Controller if both are configured.

{{define "port"}}8027{{end}}
{{define "vm_port"}}8028{{end}}
{{define "vm_port_2"}}8029{{end}}
{{define "vm_port_3"}}8030{{end}}
{{define "token"}}server_token_usb_boot_test{{end}}
{{define "appbootconfig_file"}}/mnt/appbootconfig{{end}}
{{define "network"}}n1{{end}}
{{define "ssh"}}ssh -q -o ConnectTimeout=10 -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o PasswordAuthentication=no -i {{EdenConfig "eden.tests"}}/eclient/image/cert/id_rsa root@FWD_IP -p FWD_PORT{{end}}
{{define "eclient_image"}}docker://nikolayzededa/eden-eclient:1.0.26{{end}}
{{define "test_vm"}}test-usb-boot-vm{{end}}
{{define "test_vm_2"}}test-usb-boot-vm-2{{end}}
{{define "test_vm_3"}}test-container{{end}}

[!exec:bash] stop
[!exec:sleep] stop
[!exec:ssh] stop
[!exec:chmod] stop
[!exec:jq] stop

exec chmod 600 {{EdenConfig "eden.tests"}}/eclient/image/cert/id_rsa


message 'Resetting of EVE'
# Note: eden eve reset is commented out because it removes the device state file
# which breaks subsequent eden commands. If you need a clean state, stop and
# restart eden with: ./eden stop && ./eden start && ./eden eve onboard
# eden eve reset

# Create n1 network
eden -t 1m network create 10.11.12.0/24 -n {{template "network"}}
test eden.network.test -test.v -timewait 2m ACTIVATED {{template "network"}}

# Detect USB harddrive on EVE dynamically (needed for both controller and LPS tests)
message 'Detecting USB harddrive on EVE for passthrough'
exec -t 1m bash detect-usb-harddrive.sh
source .env
stdout 'USB_ADAPTER='

# ############################################################################
# PHASE 1: DEVICE PROPERTY AND CONTROLLER API TESTS (No LPS Required)
# These tests verify boot order configuration without LPS.
# Prerequisites: Network created, USB drive detected
# ############################################################################

# ############################################################################
# DEVICE PROPERTY TESTS (TC-DEV-1 to TC-DEV-3)
# These tests verify boot_order via device config property app.boot.order
# The device property provides a device-wide default for all VMs
# ############################################################################

# ============================================================================
# TC-DEV-1: Device property app.boot.order=usb -> USB boot (Debian)
# No resolution set, no per-app boot_order - device property takes effect
# ============================================================================
message '=== TC-DEV-1: Device Property - app.boot.order=usb -> Debian (USB boot) ==='

# Ensure no FML resolution is set (so OVMF default would be USB anyway,
# but we're testing that device property is actually read)
eden controller edge-node update --config app.fml.resolution=

# Set device-wide boot order property to "usb"
eden controller edge-node update --config app.boot.order=usb

# Wait for EVE to pick up the config
message 'Waiting for EVE to apply device config...'
exec sleep 15

# Deploy test VM without per-app boot_order (should use device property)
message 'Deploying test VM without per-app boot_order (device property should apply)'
eden pod deploy -n {{template "test_vm"}} --memory=1024MB --vnc-display=1 --fml -p {{template "vm_port"}}:22 --adapters $usb_adapter https://cloud-images.ubuntu.com/releases/focal/release-20210510/ubuntu-20.04-server-cloudimg-amd64.img --networks={{template "network"}}

# USB boot VM may become unstable - use custom polling
exec -t 5m bash wait-for-running-once.sh {{template "test_vm"}}

# Get test VM UUID
exec bash get-vm-uuid.sh {{template "test_vm"}}
source .env

# Record timestamp for log filtering
exec bash record-timestamp.sh

# Verify fw_cfg is set to "usb" (from device property)
message 'TC-DEV-1a: Verify fw_cfg=usb in hypervisor config (from device property)'
exec -t 2m bash verify-hypervisor-config-v2.sh $vm_uuid usb
stdout 'fw_cfg USB boot: usb'

# Verify Debian boots (USB boot due to device property)
message 'TC-DEV-1b: Verify VM boots from USB (Debian) - device property=usb'
exec -t 2m bash verify-boot-os-v2.sh {{template "test_vm"}} debian
stdout 'BOOT OS VERIFIED'
message '=== TC-DEV-1 PASSED ==='

# Cleanup TC-DEV-1
eden pod delete {{template "test_vm"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 5m - {{template "test_vm"}}

# ============================================================================
# TC-DEV-2: Device property app.boot.order=nousb -> HDD boot (Ubuntu)
# No resolution set (OVMF default would be USB), device property overrides
# ============================================================================
message '=== TC-DEV-2: Device Property - app.boot.order=nousb -> Ubuntu (HDD boot) ==='

# Set device-wide boot order property to "nousb"
eden controller edge-node update --config app.boot.order=nousb

# Wait for EVE to pick up the config
message 'Waiting for EVE to apply device config...'
exec sleep 15

# Deploy test VM without per-app boot_order (should use device property)
message 'Deploying test VM without per-app boot_order (device property should apply)'
eden pod deploy -n {{template "test_vm"}} --memory=1024MB --vnc-display=1 --fml -p {{template "vm_port"}}:22 --adapters $usb_adapter https://cloud-images.ubuntu.com/releases/focal/release-20210510/ubuntu-20.04-server-cloudimg-amd64.img --networks={{template "network"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 10m RUNNING {{template "test_vm"}}

# Get test VM UUID
exec bash get-vm-uuid.sh {{template "test_vm"}}
source .env

# Record timestamp for log filtering
exec bash record-timestamp.sh

# Verify fw_cfg is set to "nousb" (from device property)
message 'TC-DEV-2a: Verify fw_cfg=nousb in hypervisor config (from device property)'
exec -t 2m bash verify-hypervisor-config-v2.sh $vm_uuid nousb
stdout 'fw_cfg USB boot: nousb'

# Verify Ubuntu boots (HDD boot due to device property overriding OVMF default)
message 'TC-DEV-2b: Verify VM boots from HDD (Ubuntu) - device property=nousb overrides OVMF'
exec -t 2m bash verify-boot-os-v2.sh {{template "test_vm"}} ubuntu
stdout 'BOOT OS VERIFIED'
message '=== TC-DEV-2 PASSED ==='

# Cleanup TC-DEV-2
eden pod delete {{template "test_vm"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 5m - {{template "test_vm"}}

# ============================================================================
# TC-DEV-3: Change device property on EXISTING VM (tests applyDevicePropertyBootOrder)
# This tests the scenario where app.boot.order changes while a VM is already running.
# The VM should pick up the new boot order without being redeployed.
# Flow: Deploy VM with nousb -> change to usb -> restart VM -> verify USB boot
# ============================================================================
message '=== TC-DEV-3: Device Property Change on Existing VM (applyDevicePropertyBootOrder) ==='

# Start with device property = nousb
eden controller edge-node update --config app.boot.order=nousb

# Wait for EVE to pick up the config
message 'Waiting for EVE to apply device config (nousb)...'
exec sleep 15

# Deploy test VM without per-app boot_order (uses device property = nousb)
message 'Deploying test VM with device property=nousb (initial state)'
eden pod deploy -n {{template "test_vm"}} --memory=1024MB --vnc-display=1 --fml -p {{template "vm_port"}}:22 --adapters $usb_adapter https://cloud-images.ubuntu.com/releases/focal/release-20210510/ubuntu-20.04-server-cloudimg-amd64.img --networks={{template "network"}}

# Wait for VM to be running
exec -t 5m bash wait-for-running-once.sh {{template "test_vm"}}

# Get test VM UUID
exec bash get-vm-uuid.sh {{template "test_vm"}}
source .env

# Verify initial state: fw_cfg=nousb, boots Ubuntu (HDD)
message 'TC-DEV-3a: Verify initial state - fw_cfg=nousb, Ubuntu boots'
exec -t 2m bash verify-hypervisor-config-v2.sh $vm_uuid nousb
stdout 'fw_cfg USB boot: nousb'
exec -t 2m bash verify-boot-os-v2.sh {{template "test_vm"}} ubuntu
stdout 'BOOT OS VERIFIED'

# Now change device property to usb while VM exists
message 'TC-DEV-3b: Changing device property to usb on existing VM...'
eden controller edge-node update --config app.boot.order=usb

# Wait for EVE to pick up the new property and apply it to existing apps
# This exercises applyDevicePropertyBootOrder() function
message 'Waiting for EVE to apply new device property to existing VM...'
exec sleep 20

# Restart the VM to pick up the new boot order
# (boot order change requires VM restart to take effect)
message 'TC-DEV-3c: Restarting VM to apply new boot order...'
eden pod stop {{template "test_vm"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 20m HALTED {{template "test_vm"}}
eden pod start {{template "test_vm"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 10m RUNNING {{template "test_vm"}}

# Record timestamp for log filtering
exec bash record-timestamp.sh

# Verify new state: fw_cfg=usb (changed via applyDevicePropertyBootOrder)
message 'TC-DEV-3d: Verify fw_cfg changed to usb after device property update'
exec -t 2m bash verify-hypervisor-config-v2.sh $vm_uuid usb
stdout 'fw_cfg USB boot: usb'

# Verify Debian boots (USB boot due to updated device property)
message 'TC-DEV-3e: Verify VM now boots from USB (Debian) after property change'
exec -t 2m bash verify-boot-os-v2.sh {{template "test_vm"}} debian
stdout 'BOOT OS VERIFIED'
message '=== TC-DEV-3 PASSED ==='

# Cleanup TC-DEV-3
eden pod delete {{template "test_vm"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 5m - {{template "test_vm"}}

# Reset device property for next tests
eden controller edge-node update --config app.boot.order=

message '========================================'
message 'DEVICE PROPERTY TESTS COMPLETED (TC-DEV-1 to TC-DEV-3)'
message '========================================'

# ############################################################################
# CONTROLLER API TESTS (TC-CTRL-1 to TC-CTRL-4)
# These tests verify boot_order via Controller API (VmConfig.boot_order)
# No LPS is needed - boot order is set via --boot-order flag in eden pod deploy
# and can be changed via eden pod modify --boot-order
# ############################################################################

# ============================================================================
# TC-CTRL-1: Custom resolution + boot_order=usb -> USB boot (Debian)
# fw_cfg="usb" overrides the resolution setting that would cause HDD boot

eden controller edge-node update --config app.fml.resolution=1024x768

# Wait for EVE to pick up the resolution setting
message 'Waiting for EVE to apply FML resolution setting...'
exec -t 2m bash wait-fml-resolution-applied.sh 1024x768

# Deploy test VM with boot_order=usb via controller API
message 'Deploying test VM with --boot-order=usb (FML mode, custom resolution)'
eden pod deploy -n {{template "test_vm"}} --memory=1024MB --vnc-display=1 --fml --boot-order=usb -p {{template "vm_port"}}:22 --adapters $usb_adapter https://cloud-images.ubuntu.com/releases/focal/release-20210510/ubuntu-20.04-server-cloudimg-amd64.img --networks={{template "network"}}

# USB boot VM may become unstable - use custom polling
exec -t 5m bash wait-for-running-once.sh {{template "test_vm"}}

# Get test VM UUID
exec bash get-vm-uuid.sh {{template "test_vm"}}
source .env

# Record timestamp for log filtering
exec bash record-timestamp.sh

# Verify fw_cfg is set to "usb" in hypervisor config
message 'TC-CTRL-1a: Verify fw_cfg=usb in hypervisor config'
exec -t 2m bash verify-hypervisor-config-v2.sh $vm_uuid usb
stdout 'fw_cfg USB boot: usb'

# Verify Debian boots (USB boot due to fw_cfg=usb override)
message 'TC-CTRL-1b: Verify VM boots from USB (Debian) - fw_cfg=usb overrides resolution'
exec -t 2m bash verify-boot-os-v2.sh {{template "test_vm"}} debian
stdout 'BOOT OS VERIFIED'
message '=== TC-CTRL-1 PASSED ==='

# ============================================================================
# TC-CTRL-2: Custom resolution + boot_order=nousb -> HDD boot (Ubuntu)
# fw_cfg="nousb" confirms HDD priority (same as resolution default)
# Use pod modify + restart instead of redeploy
# ============================================================================
message '=== TC-CTRL-2: Controller API - Custom resolution + boot_order=nousb -> Ubuntu (HDD boot) ==='

# Modify VM boot order via controller API (no redeploy needed)
message 'Modifying VM boot_order to nousb via pod modify'
eden pod modify {{template "test_vm"}} --boot-order=nousb

# Restart VM to apply the new boot_order setting
message 'Restarting VM to apply boot_order=nousb'
eden pod stop {{template "test_vm"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 20m HALTED {{template "test_vm"}}
eden pod start {{template "test_vm"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 10m RUNNING {{template "test_vm"}}

# Record timestamp for log filtering
exec bash record-timestamp.sh

# Verify fw_cfg is set to "nousb" in hypervisor config
message 'TC-CTRL-2a: Verify fw_cfg=nousb in hypervisor config'
exec -t 2m bash verify-hypervisor-config-v2.sh $vm_uuid nousb
stdout 'fw_cfg USB boot: nousb'

# Verify Ubuntu boots (HDD boot due to fw_cfg=nousb)
message 'TC-CTRL-2b: Verify VM boots from HDD (Ubuntu) - fw_cfg=nousb confirms HDD priority'
exec -t 2m bash verify-boot-os-v2.sh {{template "test_vm"}} ubuntu
stdout 'BOOT OS VERIFIED'
message '=== TC-CTRL-2 PASSED ==='

# ============================================================================
# TC-CTRL-3: Custom resolution + no boot_order -> HDD boot (Ubuntu)
# Default behavior with resolution set: OVMF boots from HDD (no fw_cfg)
# Need to redeploy to get a VM without boot_order set
# ============================================================================
message '=== TC-CTRL-3: Controller API - Custom resolution + no boot_order -> Ubuntu (HDD boot) ==='

# Delete current VM and redeploy without --boot-order flag
message 'Redeploying VM without --boot-order (to test default behavior)'
eden pod delete {{template "test_vm"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 5m - {{template "test_vm"}}

eden pod deploy -n {{template "test_vm"}} --memory=1024MB --vnc-display=1 --fml -p {{template "vm_port"}}:22 --adapters $usb_adapter https://cloud-images.ubuntu.com/releases/focal/release-20210510/ubuntu-20.04-server-cloudimg-amd64.img --networks={{template "network"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 10m RUNNING {{template "test_vm"}}

# Get test VM UUID (may have changed after redeploy)
exec bash get-vm-uuid.sh {{template "test_vm"}}
source .env

# Record timestamp for log filtering
exec bash record-timestamp.sh

# Verify NO fw_cfg is set (boot_order is empty/not set)
message 'TC-CTRL-3a: Verify NO fw_cfg in hypervisor config (no boot_order set)'
exec -t 2m bash verify-hypervisor-config-v2.sh $vm_uuid none
stdout 'fw_cfg USB boot: not set'

# Verify Ubuntu boots (HDD boot due to resolution, no fw_cfg override)
message 'TC-CTRL-3b: Verify VM boots from HDD (Ubuntu) - default with resolution set'
exec -t 2m bash verify-boot-os-v2.sh {{template "test_vm"}} ubuntu
stdout 'BOOT OS VERIFIED'
message '=== TC-CTRL-3 PASSED ==='

# ============================================================================
# TC-CTRL-4: No resolution + boot_order=nousb -> HDD boot (Ubuntu)
# fw_cfg="nousb" overrides OVMF default (which would boot USB without resolution)
# Need to change resolution AND boot_order
# ============================================================================
message '=== TC-CTRL-4: Controller API - No resolution + boot_order=nousb -> Ubuntu (HDD boot) ==='

# Remove FML resolution
eden controller edge-node update --config app.fml.resolution=

# Wait for EVE to pick up the resolution removal
message 'Waiting for EVE to apply FML resolution removal...'
exec -t 2m bash wait-fml-resolution-applied.sh ""

# Modify VM boot order via controller API
message 'Modifying VM boot_order to nousb via pod modify'
eden pod modify {{template "test_vm"}} --boot-order=nousb

# Restart VM to apply the new settings (resolution change + boot_order)
message 'Restarting VM to apply boot_order=nousb with no resolution'
eden pod stop {{template "test_vm"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 20m HALTED {{template "test_vm"}}
eden pod start {{template "test_vm"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 10m RUNNING {{template "test_vm"}}

# Record timestamp for log filtering
exec bash record-timestamp.sh

# Verify fw_cfg is set to "nousb" in hypervisor config
message 'TC-CTRL-4a: Verify fw_cfg=nousb in hypervisor config'
exec -t 2m bash verify-hypervisor-config-v2.sh $vm_uuid nousb
stdout 'fw_cfg USB boot: nousb'

# Verify Ubuntu boots (HDD boot due to fw_cfg=nousb overriding OVMF default)
message 'TC-CTRL-4b: Verify VM boots from HDD (Ubuntu) - fw_cfg=nousb overrides OVMF default'
exec -t 2m bash verify-boot-os-v2.sh {{template "test_vm"}} ubuntu
stdout 'BOOT OS VERIFIED'
message '=== TC-CTRL-4 PASSED ==='

# Cleanup controller tests and prepare for next tests
eden pod delete {{template "test_vm"}}

message '========================================'
message 'CONTROLLER API TESTS COMPLETED (TC-CTRL-1 to TC-CTRL-4)'
message '========================================'

# ############################################################################
# PRIORITY TESTS (TC-PRIO-1 to TC-PRIO-3)
# These tests verify the precedence order: LPS > Controller API > Device Property
# Each test sets conflicting values at different levels to verify priority
# ############################################################################

# ============================================================================
# TC-PRIO-1: Device=usb, Controller=nousb -> HDD boot (Controller overrides Device)
# Device property says USB, but Controller per-app setting says nousb
# Expected: Ubuntu boots (Controller wins over Device property)
# ============================================================================
message '=== TC-PRIO-1: Priority - Device=usb, Controller=nousb -> Ubuntu (Controller wins) ==='

# Set device property to usb (would cause USB boot if used)
eden controller edge-node update --config app.boot.order=usb

# Wait for EVE to pick up the config
message 'Waiting for EVE to apply device config...'
exec sleep 15

# Deploy test VM WITH per-app boot_order=nousb (should override device property)
message 'Deploying test VM with --boot-order=nousb (should override device property=usb)'
eden pod deploy -n {{template "test_vm"}} --memory=1024MB --vnc-display=1 --fml --boot-order=nousb -p {{template "vm_port"}}:22 --adapters $usb_adapter https://cloud-images.ubuntu.com/releases/focal/release-20210510/ubuntu-20.04-server-cloudimg-amd64.img --networks={{template "network"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 10m RUNNING {{template "test_vm"}}

# Get test VM UUID
exec bash get-vm-uuid.sh {{template "test_vm"}}
source .env

# Record timestamp for log filtering
exec bash record-timestamp.sh

# Verify fw_cfg is set to "nousb" (from Controller, not device property)
message 'TC-PRIO-1a: Verify fw_cfg=nousb (Controller overrides device property=usb)'
exec -t 2m bash verify-hypervisor-config-v2.sh $vm_uuid nousb
stdout 'fw_cfg USB boot: nousb'

# Verify Ubuntu boots (Controller wins, device property ignored)
message 'TC-PRIO-1b: Verify VM boots from HDD (Ubuntu) - Controller beats Device property'
exec -t 2m bash verify-boot-os-v2.sh {{template "test_vm"}} ubuntu
stdout 'BOOT OS VERIFIED'
message '=== TC-PRIO-1 PASSED ==='

# Keep VM running for next test (we'll add LPS override)

message '========================================'
message 'PRIORITY TESTS COMPLETED (TC-PRIO-1)'
message '========================================'

# Clean up device property before LPS tests
eden controller edge-node update --config app.boot.order=

# Cleanup priority tests
eden pod delete {{template "test_vm"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 5m - {{template "test_vm"}}

# ############################################################################
# PHASE 2: LPS TESTS (Local Profile Server Required)
# These tests require LPS to be deployed, so they run here after LPS setup
# ############################################################################

# ############################################################################
# LPS DEPLOYMENT
# Deploy local-manager container which simulates LPS functionality
# ############################################################################

# Deploy local-manager (LPS simulator)
eden pod deploy -n local-manager --memory=512MB {{template "eclient_image"}} -p {{template "port"}}:22 --networks={{template "network"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 10m RUNNING local-manager

# Wait for ssh access to local-manager
exec -t 5m bash wait-ssh.sh {{template "port"}}

# Start local manager application with VM config support
exec -t 1m bash local-manager-start.sh

# Obtain local-manager IP address
exec -t 2m bash get-app-ip.sh local-manager
source .env

# Configure local server
eden controller edge-node update --device profile_server_token={{template "token"}}
eden controller edge-node update --device local_profile_server=$app_ip:8888

# ============================================================================
# STEP 0: Verify LPS endpoint is working
# ============================================================================
message 'STEP 0: Verify LPS boot config endpoint is accessible'
exec -t 2m bash verify-lps-endpoint.sh
! stdout 'ENDPOINT_ERROR'
stdout 'LPS endpoint verified'

# USB detection already done before controller tests, reuse $usb_adapter from .env

# ############################################################################
# MAIN CUSTOMER USE CASE TEST (TC-INSTALL-1)
# This is the PRIMARY customer scenario: Install OS to VM in FML mode from USB
# The workflow uses the priority hierarchy: LPS > Controller > Device Property
#   - Device property app.boot.order=nousb: Default HDD boot
#   - LPS bootOrderConfig=usb: Temporarily enable USB boot for installation
#   - LPS bootOrderConfig=UNSPECIFIED: Fall back to device property (post-install)
#
# Customer setup: 3 apps running - 2 FML VMs and 1 non-FML container
# We verify the primary FML VM with USB passthrough (test_vm)
# ############################################################################

# ============================================================================
# TC-INSTALL-1: OS Installation Workflow Simulation (Customer Use Case)
# Simulates the customer use case of installing OS from USB to VM in FML mode:
#   Step 0: Deploy 3 apps (2 FML VMs + 1 container) - customer typical setup
#   Step 1: Device property=nousb -> HDD boot (normal operation)
#   Step 2: LPS=usb overrides device property -> USB boot (install OS)
#   Step 3: LPS=UNSPECIFIED -> falls back to device property -> HDD boot
#
# This is the EXACT workflow requested by the customer.
# ============================================================================
message '=== TC-INSTALL-1: OS Installation Workflow (Device=nousb, LPS=usb, LPS=UNSPECIFIED) ==='
message 'This test validates the main customer use case for USB boot priority feature'
message 'Customer setup: 2 FML VMs + 1 container running simultaneously'

# Clean LPS state before test
exec -t 1m bash clean-lps-state.sh

# Set FML resolution for FML mode
eden controller edge-node update --config app.fml.resolution=1024x768

# Set device property to nousb (this is the default HDD boot policy)
message 'Setting device property app.boot.order=nousb (default HDD boot policy)'
eden controller edge-node update --config app.boot.order=nousb

# Wait for EVE to pick up the config
message 'Waiting for EVE to apply device config...'
exec sleep 15
exec -t 2m bash wait-fml-resolution-applied.sh 1024x768

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Step 0: Deploy 3 apps - typical customer setup
# - test_vm: FML VM with USB passthrough (the one we'll test OS installation on)
# - test_vm_2: Second FML VM (no USB, just to simulate customer workload)
# - test_vm_3: Non-FML container (to verify boot order doesn't affect containers)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
message 'TC-INSTALL-1 Step 0: Deploy 3 apps (2 FML VMs + 1 container)'

# Deploy primary FML VM with USB passthrough
message 'Deploying primary FML VM with USB passthrough (test_vm)'
eden pod deploy -n {{template "test_vm"}} --memory=1024MB --vnc-display=1 --fml -p {{template "vm_port"}}:22 --adapters $usb_adapter https://cloud-images.ubuntu.com/releases/focal/release-20210510/ubuntu-20.04-server-cloudimg-amd64.img --networks={{template "network"}}

# Deploy second FML VM (no USB)
message 'Deploying second FML VM (test_vm_2)'
eden pod deploy -n {{template "test_vm_2"}} --memory=512MB --vnc-display=2 --fml -p {{template "vm_port_2"}}:22 https://cloud-images.ubuntu.com/releases/focal/release-20210510/ubuntu-20.04-server-cloudimg-amd64.img --networks={{template "network"}}

# Deploy non-FML container
message 'Deploying non-FML container (test_vm_3)'
eden pod deploy -n {{template "test_vm_3"}} --memory=256MB docker://nginx:alpine --networks={{template "network"}}

# Wait for all apps to be running
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 30m RUNNING {{template "test_vm"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 30m RUNNING {{template "test_vm_2"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 30m RUNNING {{template "test_vm_3"}}

message 'All 3 apps deployed and running'

# Get primary test VM UUID (the one we'll verify)
exec bash get-vm-uuid.sh {{template "test_vm"}}
source .env

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Step 1: Verify default HDD boot (device property=nousb in effect)
# This simulates normal operation before OS installation
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
message 'TC-INSTALL-1 Step 1: Verify HDD boot (device property=nousb)'

# Record timestamp for log filtering
exec bash record-timestamp.sh

# Verify fw_cfg is set to "nousb" (from device property)
message 'TC-INSTALL-1a: Verify fw_cfg=nousb (from device property)'
exec -t 2m bash verify-hypervisor-config-v2.sh $vm_uuid nousb
stdout 'fw_cfg USB boot: nousb'

# Verify appbootinfo shows device property as source
message 'TC-INSTALL-1a2: Verify appbootinfo shows DEVICE_PROPERTY as source'
exec -t 3m bash verify-appbootinfo.sh $vm_uuid BOOT_ORDER_NOUSB BOOT_ORDER_SOURCE_DEVICE_PROPERTY
stdout 'APPBOOTINFO_VERIFIED'

# Verify Ubuntu boots from HDD (device property enforces HDD boot)
message 'TC-INSTALL-1b: Verify VM boots from HDD (Ubuntu) - normal operation'
exec -t 2m bash verify-boot-os-v2.sh {{template "test_vm"}} ubuntu
stdout 'BOOT OS VERIFIED'
message 'TC-INSTALL-1 Step 1 PASSED: Default HDD boot via device property works'

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Step 2: Set LPS bootOrderConfig=usb to boot from USB (OS installation)
# Customer uses LPS to temporarily enable USB boot for OS installation
# LPS overrides device property (priority: LPS > Controller > Device)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
message 'TC-INSTALL-1 Step 2: Set LPS bootOrderConfig=usb (USB boot for installation)'
exec -t 2m bash set-vm-boot-order.sh $vm_uuid usb
exec -t 2m bash wait-vm-config-applied.sh

# Verify appbootinfo shows LPS as source BEFORE restart
message 'TC-INSTALL-1c0: Verify appbootinfo shows LPS as source BEFORE restart'
exec -t 3m bash verify-appbootinfo.sh $vm_uuid BOOT_ORDER_USB BOOT_ORDER_SOURCE_LPS
stdout 'APPBOOTINFO_VERIFIED'

# Restart VM to boot from USB (simulates reboot for installation)
message 'Restarting VM to boot from USB (installation mode)'
eden pod stop {{template "test_vm"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 20m HALTED {{template "test_vm"}}
eden pod start {{template "test_vm"}}
exec -t 5m bash wait-for-running-once.sh {{template "test_vm"}}

# Record timestamp for log filtering
exec bash record-timestamp.sh

# Verify fw_cfg is set to "usb" (LPS overrides device property)
message 'TC-INSTALL-1c: Verify fw_cfg=usb (LPS overrides device property=nousb)'
exec -t 2m bash verify-hypervisor-config-v2.sh $vm_uuid usb
stdout 'fw_cfg USB boot: usb'

# Verify appbootinfo shows LPS as source after restart
message 'TC-INSTALL-1c2: Verify appbootinfo shows LPS as source'
exec -t 3m bash verify-appbootinfo.sh $vm_uuid BOOT_ORDER_USB BOOT_ORDER_SOURCE_LPS
stdout 'APPBOOTINFO_VERIFIED'

# Verify Debian boots from USB (LPS forces USB boot for installation)
message 'TC-INSTALL-1d: Verify VM boots from USB (Debian) - installation mode'
exec -t 2m bash verify-boot-os-v2.sh {{template "test_vm"}} debian
stdout 'BOOT OS VERIFIED'
message 'TC-INSTALL-1 Step 2 PASSED: LPS USB boot for installation works'

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Step 3: Set LPS to UNSPECIFIED to fall back to device property (post-install)
# Customer sets LPS boot order to UNSPECIFIED after installation completes
# VM falls back to device property=nousb -> HDD boot
# Using "unspecified" which maps to BOOT_ORDER_UNSPECIFIED enum
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
message 'TC-INSTALL-1 Step 3: Set LPS=UNSPECIFIED (fall back to device property=nousb)'
exec -t 2m bash set-vm-boot-order.sh $vm_uuid unspecified
exec -t 2m bash wait-vm-config-applied.sh

# Verify appbootinfo shows device property as source BEFORE restart
message 'TC-INSTALL-1e0: Verify appbootinfo shows DEVICE_PROPERTY BEFORE restart'
exec -t 3m bash verify-appbootinfo.sh $vm_uuid BOOT_ORDER_NOUSB BOOT_ORDER_SOURCE_DEVICE_PROPERTY
stdout 'APPBOOTINFO_VERIFIED'

# Restart VM to boot from HDD (post-installation)
message 'Restarting VM to boot from HDD (post-installation)'
eden pod stop {{template "test_vm"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 20m HALTED {{template "test_vm"}}
eden pod start {{template "test_vm"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 10m RUNNING {{template "test_vm"}}

# Record timestamp for log filtering
exec bash record-timestamp.sh

# Verify fw_cfg is set to "nousb" (back to device property after LPS=UNSPECIFIED)
message 'TC-INSTALL-1e: Verify fw_cfg=nousb (device property after LPS=UNSPECIFIED)'
exec -t 2m bash verify-hypervisor-config-v2.sh $vm_uuid nousb
stdout 'fw_cfg USB boot: nousb'

# Verify appbootinfo shows device property as source after restart
message 'TC-INSTALL-1e2: Verify appbootinfo shows DEVICE_PROPERTY after restart'
exec -t 3m bash verify-appbootinfo.sh $vm_uuid BOOT_ORDER_NOUSB BOOT_ORDER_SOURCE_DEVICE_PROPERTY
stdout 'APPBOOTINFO_VERIFIED'

# Verify Ubuntu boots from HDD (device property takes effect after LPS=UNSPECIFIED)
message 'TC-INSTALL-1f: Verify VM boots from HDD (Ubuntu) - post-installation'
exec -t 2m bash verify-boot-os-v2.sh {{template "test_vm"}} ubuntu
stdout 'BOOT OS VERIFIED'
message 'TC-INSTALL-1 Step 3 PASSED: HDD boot after installation works'

message '=== TC-INSTALL-1 PASSED: Complete OS installation workflow validated ==='
message '  - Step 0: 3 apps deployed (2 FML VMs + 1 container) - VERIFIED'
message '  - Step 1: Device property=nousb -> HDD boot (Ubuntu) - VERIFIED'
message '  - Step 2: LPS=usb overrides -> USB boot (Debian) - VERIFIED'
message '  - Step 3: LPS=UNSPECIFIED -> Device property -> HDD boot (Ubuntu) - VERIFIED'
message 'Customer use case for USB boot priority feature is fully validated!'

# Cleanup TC-INSTALL-1 - delete all VMs and clean device property for next tests
eden pod delete {{template "test_vm"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 5m - {{template "test_vm"}}
eden pod delete {{template "test_vm_2"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 5m - {{template "test_vm_2"}}
eden pod delete {{template "test_vm_3"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 5m - {{template "test_vm_3"}}
eden controller edge-node update --config app.boot.order=

message '========================================'
message 'MAIN CUSTOMER USE CASE TEST COMPLETED (TC-INSTALL-1)'
message '========================================'

# ############################################################################
# PRIORITY TESTS WITH LPS (TC-PRIO-2 to TC-PRIO-3)
# These tests require LPS to be deployed, so they run here after LPS setup
# ############################################################################

# ============================================================================
# TC-PRIO-2: Device=usb, Controller=nousb, LPS=usb -> USB boot (LPS wins)
# All three levels are set to conflicting values
# Expected: Debian boots (LPS has highest priority)
# ============================================================================
message '=== TC-PRIO-2: Priority - Device=usb, Controller=nousb, LPS=usb -> Debian (LPS wins) ==='

# Clean LPS state before test
exec -t 1m bash clean-lps-state.sh

# Set device property to usb
eden controller edge-node update --config app.boot.order=usb

# Wait for EVE to pick up the config
message 'Waiting for EVE to apply device config...'
exec sleep 15

# Deploy test VM WITH per-app boot_order=nousb (Controller says nousb)
message 'Deploying test VM with --boot-order=nousb (Controller=nousb, Device=usb)'
eden pod deploy -n {{template "test_vm"}} --memory=1024MB --vnc-display=1 --fml --boot-order=nousb -p {{template "vm_port"}}:22 --adapters $usb_adapter https://cloud-images.ubuntu.com/releases/focal/release-20210510/ubuntu-20.04-server-cloudimg-amd64.img --networks={{template "network"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 10m RUNNING {{template "test_vm"}}

# Get test VM UUID
exec bash get-vm-uuid.sh {{template "test_vm"}}
source .env

# At this point: Device=usb, Controller=nousb, LPS=unset
# Without LPS, Controller should win and VM boots from HDD (Ubuntu)
# Verify this baseline before adding LPS override

# Record timestamp for log filtering
exec bash record-timestamp.sh

# Verify fw_cfg is set to "nousb" (Controller wins over device property for now)
message 'TC-PRIO-2a: Baseline - Controller=nousb wins over Device=usb (before LPS)'
exec -t 2m bash verify-hypervisor-config-v2.sh $vm_uuid nousb
stdout 'fw_cfg USB boot: nousb'

# Verify Ubuntu boots (Controller wins)
message 'TC-PRIO-2b: Baseline - VM boots from HDD (Ubuntu) before LPS override'
exec -t 2m bash verify-boot-os-v2.sh {{template "test_vm"}} ubuntu
stdout 'BOOT OS VERIFIED'

# Now set LPS to usb (should override both Device and Controller)
message 'TC-PRIO-2c: Setting LPS bootOrderConfig=usb to override Controller=nousb'
exec -t 2m bash set-vm-boot-order.sh $vm_uuid usb
exec -t 2m bash wait-vm-config-applied.sh

# Restart VM to apply LPS setting
message 'Restarting VM to apply LPS bootOrderConfig=usb'
eden pod stop {{template "test_vm"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 20m HALTED {{template "test_vm"}}
eden pod start {{template "test_vm"}}
exec -t 5m bash wait-for-running-once.sh {{template "test_vm"}}

# Record timestamp for log filtering
exec bash record-timestamp.sh

# Verify fw_cfg is now "usb" (LPS overrides Controller)
message 'TC-PRIO-2d: Verify fw_cfg=usb (LPS overrides Controller=nousb and Device=usb)'
exec -t 2m bash verify-hypervisor-config-v2.sh $vm_uuid usb
stdout 'fw_cfg USB boot: usb'

# Verify Debian boots (LPS wins)
message 'TC-PRIO-2e: Verify VM boots from USB (Debian) - LPS beats Controller and Device'
exec -t 2m bash verify-boot-os-v2.sh {{template "test_vm"}} debian
stdout 'BOOT OS VERIFIED'

# Verify appbootinfo reports LPS as the source
message 'TC-PRIO-2f: Verify appbootinfo shows source=LPS'
exec -t 3m bash verify-appbootinfo.sh $vm_uuid BOOT_ORDER_USB BOOT_ORDER_SOURCE_LPS
stdout 'APPBOOTINFO_VERIFIED'
message '=== TC-PRIO-2 PASSED ==='

# ============================================================================
# TC-PRIO-4: LPS clear -> fallback to Controller
# This tests that when LPS clears its override, the app immediately falls back
# to the Controller boot order (without needing a new controller config).
# Setup: Controller=nousb, LPS=usb (from TC-PRIO-2)
# Action: Remove app from LPS response (clear LPS override)
# Expected: Ubuntu boots (falls back to Controller=nousb)
# IMPORTANT: We verify appbootinfo BEFORE restart to ensure the value is correct
# at the moment of decision, not after a restart/reparse.
# ============================================================================
message '=== TC-PRIO-4: LPS Clear - Falls back to Controller ==='

# At this point from TC-PRIO-2: Controller=nousb, LPS=usb, VM is running with USB boot
# Now clear LPS by removing this app from the response
message 'TC-PRIO-4a: Clearing LPS override (removing app from LPS response)'
exec -t 2m bash set-lps-config-for-other-app.sh
exec -t 2m bash wait-vm-config-applied.sh

# CRITICAL: Verify appbootinfo BEFORE restart - this catches the bug where
# the value isn't updated until next controller config parse
message 'TC-PRIO-4b: Verify appbootinfo shows Controller BEFORE restart (catches cache bug)'
exec -t 3m bash verify-appbootinfo.sh $vm_uuid BOOT_ORDER_NOUSB BOOT_ORDER_SOURCE_CONTROLLER
stdout 'APPBOOTINFO_VERIFIED'

# Restart VM to apply the cleared LPS setting
message 'TC-PRIO-4c: Restarting VM to apply LPS clear'
eden pod stop {{template "test_vm"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 20m HALTED {{template "test_vm"}}
eden pod start {{template "test_vm"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 10m RUNNING {{template "test_vm"}}

# Record timestamp for log filtering
exec bash record-timestamp.sh

# Verify fw_cfg is now "nousb" (LPS cleared, falls back to Controller)
message 'TC-PRIO-4d: Verify fw_cfg=nousb (LPS cleared, Controller wins)'
exec -t 2m bash verify-hypervisor-config-v2.sh $vm_uuid nousb
stdout 'fw_cfg USB boot: nousb'

# Verify Ubuntu boots (Controller wins after LPS clear)
message 'TC-PRIO-4e: Verify VM boots from HDD (Ubuntu) - Controller wins after LPS clear'
exec -t 2m bash verify-boot-os-v2.sh {{template "test_vm"}} ubuntu
stdout 'BOOT OS VERIFIED'

# Verify appbootinfo again after restart (should still be Controller)
message 'TC-PRIO-4f: Verify appbootinfo shows source=CONTROLLER after restart'
exec -t 3m bash verify-appbootinfo.sh $vm_uuid BOOT_ORDER_NOUSB BOOT_ORDER_SOURCE_CONTROLLER
stdout 'APPBOOTINFO_VERIFIED'
message '=== TC-PRIO-4 PASSED ==='

# Cleanup TC-PRIO-4
eden pod delete {{template "test_vm"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 5m - {{template "test_vm"}}

# ============================================================================
# TC-PRIO-3: Device=nousb, Controller="", LPS="" -> HDD boot (Device default used)
# Only device property is set, Controller and LPS are empty
# Expected: Ubuntu boots (Device property is used as fallback)
# ============================================================================
message '=== TC-PRIO-3: Priority - Device=nousb, Controller="", LPS="" -> Ubuntu (Device fallback) ==='

# Clean LPS state before test
exec -t 1m bash clean-lps-state.sh

# Set device property to nousb
eden controller edge-node update --config app.boot.order=nousb

# Wait for EVE to pick up the config
message 'Waiting for EVE to apply device config...'
exec sleep 15

# Deploy test VM WITHOUT per-app boot_order (Controller empty)
# LPS is also not set for this app
message 'Deploying test VM without per-app boot_order (Device=nousb should apply)'
eden pod deploy -n {{template "test_vm"}} --memory=1024MB --vnc-display=1 --fml -p {{template "vm_port"}}:22 --adapters $usb_adapter https://cloud-images.ubuntu.com/releases/focal/release-20210510/ubuntu-20.04-server-cloudimg-amd64.img --networks={{template "network"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 10m RUNNING {{template "test_vm"}}

# Get test VM UUID
exec bash get-vm-uuid.sh {{template "test_vm"}}
source .env

# Record timestamp for log filtering
exec bash record-timestamp.sh

# Verify fw_cfg is set to "nousb" (from device property as fallback)
message 'TC-PRIO-3a: Verify fw_cfg=nousb (Device property used as fallback)'
exec -t 2m bash verify-hypervisor-config-v2.sh $vm_uuid nousb
stdout 'fw_cfg USB boot: nousb'

# Verify Ubuntu boots (Device property fallback)
message 'TC-PRIO-3b: Verify VM boots from HDD (Ubuntu) - Device property as fallback'
exec -t 2m bash verify-boot-os-v2.sh {{template "test_vm"}} ubuntu
stdout 'BOOT OS VERIFIED'

# Verify appbootinfo reports DeviceProperty as the source
message 'TC-PRIO-3c: Verify appbootinfo shows source=DEVICE_PROPERTY'
exec -t 3m bash verify-appbootinfo.sh $vm_uuid BOOT_ORDER_NOUSB BOOT_ORDER_SOURCE_DEVICE_PROPERTY
stdout 'APPBOOTINFO_VERIFIED'

# ============================================================================
# TC-PRIO-5: LPS explicit UNSPECIFIED -> fallback to Device Property
# This tests that when LPS sends explicit BOOT_ORDER_UNSPECIFIED, the app
# correctly falls back to Device Property (since Controller is empty).
# Reuses the VM from TC-PRIO-3 which has Controller="", Device=nousb
# ============================================================================
message '=== TC-PRIO-5: LPS explicit UNSPECIFIED - Falls back to DeviceProperty ==='

# First set LPS to USB to establish an LPS override
message 'TC-PRIO-5a: Setting LPS=USB to establish override'
exec -t 2m bash set-vm-boot-order.sh $vm_uuid usb
exec -t 2m bash wait-vm-config-applied.sh

# Verify appbootinfo BEFORE restart - LPS should take effect immediately
message 'TC-PRIO-5a2: Verify appbootinfo shows LPS BEFORE restart'
exec -t 3m bash verify-appbootinfo.sh $vm_uuid BOOT_ORDER_USB BOOT_ORDER_SOURCE_LPS
stdout 'APPBOOTINFO_VERIFIED'

# Restart to apply LPS=USB
eden pod stop {{template "test_vm"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 20m HALTED {{template "test_vm"}}
eden pod start {{template "test_vm"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 10m RUNNING {{template "test_vm"}}

# Verify LPS=USB took effect
message 'TC-PRIO-5b: Verify LPS=USB took effect'
exec -t 2m bash verify-hypervisor-config-v2.sh $vm_uuid usb
stdout 'fw_cfg USB boot: usb'

# Now send explicit UNSPECIFIED (different from removing from response)
message 'TC-PRIO-5c: Sending LPS explicit BOOT_ORDER_UNSPECIFIED'
exec -t 2m bash set-vm-boot-order.sh $vm_uuid ""
exec -t 2m bash wait-vm-config-applied.sh

# CRITICAL: Verify appbootinfo BEFORE restart - this catches the bug where
# explicit UNSPECIFIED doesn't properly clear the LPS cache
message 'TC-PRIO-5d: Verify appbootinfo shows DeviceProperty BEFORE restart (catches cache bug)'
exec -t 3m bash verify-appbootinfo.sh $vm_uuid BOOT_ORDER_NOUSB BOOT_ORDER_SOURCE_DEVICE_PROPERTY
stdout 'APPBOOTINFO_VERIFIED'

# Restart to apply LPS clear
eden pod stop {{template "test_vm"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 20m HALTED {{template "test_vm"}}
eden pod start {{template "test_vm"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 10m RUNNING {{template "test_vm"}}

# Record timestamp for log filtering
exec bash record-timestamp.sh

# Verify fw_cfg is now "nousb" (LPS=UNSPECIFIED, falls back to Device)
message 'TC-PRIO-5e: Verify fw_cfg=nousb (LPS UNSPECIFIED, falls back to Device)'
exec -t 2m bash verify-hypervisor-config-v2.sh $vm_uuid nousb
stdout 'fw_cfg USB boot: nousb'

# Verify Ubuntu boots
message 'TC-PRIO-5f: Verify VM boots from HDD (Ubuntu) - Device wins after LPS UNSPECIFIED'
exec -t 2m bash verify-boot-os-v2.sh {{template "test_vm"}} ubuntu
stdout 'BOOT OS VERIFIED'

# Verify appbootinfo again after restart (should still be DeviceProperty)
message 'TC-PRIO-5g: Verify appbootinfo shows source=DEVICE_PROPERTY after restart'
exec -t 3m bash verify-appbootinfo.sh $vm_uuid BOOT_ORDER_NOUSB BOOT_ORDER_SOURCE_DEVICE_PROPERTY
stdout 'APPBOOTINFO_VERIFIED'
message '=== TC-PRIO-5 PASSED ==='

message '=== TC-PRIO-3 PASSED ==='

eden pod delete {{template "test_vm"}}

# Clean up device property before regular LPS tests
eden controller edge-node update --config app.boot.order=

message '========================================'
message 'ALL PRIORITY TESTS COMPLETED (TC-PRIO-1 to TC-PRIO-3)'
message '========================================'

# ############################################################################
# EMPTY STRING EDGE CASE TESTS (TC-EMPTY-1 to TC-EMPTY-5)
# These tests verify that empty string ("") means "no override" at each level
# and that LPS 404 / app-not-in-response / usb_boot="" are handled correctly
# ############################################################################

# ============================================================================
# TC-EMPTY-1: Device=usb, Controller="" -> USB boot (Controller empty = no override)
# Controller has empty boot_order, should fall back to Device property
# Expected: Debian boots (Device property usb is used)
# ============================================================================
message '=== TC-EMPTY-1: Empty String - Device=usb, Controller="" -> Debian (Device used) ==='

# Set device property to usb
eden controller edge-node update --config app.boot.order=usb

# Wait for EVE to pick up the config
message 'Waiting for EVE to apply device config...'
exec sleep 15

# Deploy test VM WITHOUT per-app boot_order (Controller empty)
message 'Deploying test VM without --boot-order (Controller="", Device=usb)'
eden pod deploy -n {{template "test_vm"}} --memory=1024MB --vnc-display=1 --fml -p {{template "vm_port"}}:22 --adapters $usb_adapter https://cloud-images.ubuntu.com/releases/focal/release-20210510/ubuntu-20.04-server-cloudimg-amd64.img --networks={{template "network"}}

# USB boot VM may become unstable - use custom polling
exec -t 5m bash wait-for-running-once.sh {{template "test_vm"}}

# Get test VM UUID
exec bash get-vm-uuid.sh {{template "test_vm"}}
source .env

# Record timestamp for log filtering
exec bash record-timestamp.sh

# Verify fw_cfg is set to "usb" (from device property, Controller was empty)
message 'TC-EMPTY-1a: Verify fw_cfg=usb (Controller="" falls back to Device=usb)'
exec -t 2m bash verify-hypervisor-config-v2.sh $vm_uuid usb
stdout 'fw_cfg USB boot: usb'

# Verify Debian boots (Device property used because Controller is empty)
message 'TC-EMPTY-1b: Verify VM boots from USB (Debian) - Controller empty, Device wins'
exec -t 2m bash verify-boot-os-v2.sh {{template "test_vm"}} debian
stdout 'BOOT OS VERIFIED'
message '=== TC-EMPTY-1 PASSED ==='

# Cleanup TC-EMPTY-1
eden pod delete {{template "test_vm"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 5m - {{template "test_vm"}}

# ============================================================================
# TC-EMPTY-2: Device=usb, Controller=nousb, LPS usb_boot="" -> HDD boot
# LPS has app in response but with EXPLICIT empty usb_boot=""
# Expected: Ubuntu boots (LPS usb_boot="" = no override, Controller wins)
# ============================================================================
message '=== TC-EMPTY-2: LPS usb_boot="" - Device=usb, Controller=nousb, LPS="" -> Ubuntu ==='

# Device property is still usb from previous test

# Deploy test VM WITH per-app boot_order=nousb
message 'Deploying test VM with --boot-order=nousb (Controller=nousb, Device=usb)'

# Record timestamp for log filtering

# Verify baseline: Controller=nousb wins over Device=usb

exec -t 2m bash verify-hypervisor-config-v2.sh $vm_uuid nousb
stdout 'fw_cfg USB boot: nousb'

# Now set LPS to EXPLICIT empty string for this app (should NOT override)
# This sends: { "app_configs": [{ "id": "<uuid>", "usb_boot": "" }] }
message 'TC-EMPTY-2b: Setting LPS usb_boot="" explicitly (empty = no override)'
exec -t 2m bash set-vm-boot-order.sh $vm_uuid ""
exec -t 2m bash wait-vm-config-applied.sh

# Verify appbootinfo shows Controller as source (LPS usb_boot="" means no override)
exec -t 3m bash verify-appbootinfo.sh $vm_uuid BOOT_ORDER_NOUSB BOOT_ORDER_SOURCE_CONTROLLER

# Restart VM to apply
message 'Restarting VM to verify LPS usb_boot="" does not override Controller'
eden pod stop {{template "test_vm"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 20m HALTED {{template "test_vm"}}
eden pod start {{template "test_vm"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 10m RUNNING {{template "test_vm"}}

# Record timestamp for log filtering
exec bash record-timestamp.sh

# Verify fw_cfg is still "nousb" (LPS usb_boot="" = no override, Controller wins)
message 'TC-EMPTY-2c: Verify fw_cfg=nousb (LPS usb_boot="" does not override Controller)'
exec -t 2m bash verify-hypervisor-config-v2.sh $vm_uuid nousb
stdout 'fw_cfg USB boot: nousb'

# Verify Ubuntu boots (Controller wins because LPS usb_boot is empty)
message 'TC-EMPTY-2d: Verify VM boots from HDD (Ubuntu) - LPS usb_boot="", Controller wins'
exec -t 2m bash verify-boot-os-v2.sh {{template "test_vm"}} ubuntu
stdout 'BOOT OS VERIFIED'
message '=== TC-EMPTY-2 PASSED ==='

# Set bootOrderConfig=usb via LPS

# ============================================================================
# TC10: LPS Address Change - Verify EVE re-fetches config when LPS address changes
# This tests the pause/resume mechanism in LocalCmdAgent.UpdateLpsConfig()
# ============================================================================
message '=== TC10: LPS address change triggers config re-fetch ==='

# Clean LPS state before test
exec -t 1m bash clean-lps-state.sh

# Ensure VM is deployed
eden pod delete {{template "test_vm"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 5m - {{template "test_vm"}}
eden pod deploy -n {{template "test_vm"}} --memory=1024MB --vnc-display=1 --fml -p {{template "vm_port"}}:22 --adapters $usb_adapter https://cloud-images.ubuntu.com/releases/focal/release-20210510/ubuntu-20.04-server-cloudimg-amd64.img --networks={{template "network"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 10m RUNNING {{template "test_vm"}}

exec bash get-vm-uuid.sh {{template "test_vm"}}
source .env

# Set initial boot order config
exec -t 2m bash set-vm-boot-order.sh $vm_uuid usb
exec -t 2m bash wait-vm-config-applied.sh

# Verify appbootinfo shows LPS as source with USB boot order
exec -t 3m bash verify-appbootinfo.sh $vm_uuid BOOT_ORDER_USB BOOT_ORDER_SOURCE_LPS

# Verify EVE received the config
message 'TC10a: Verify EVE received bootOrderConfig=usb'
exec -t 2m bash verify-eve-received-config-v2.sh $vm_uuid usb
stdout 'EVE received boot order config'

# Now change LPS address to a different value (simulating LPS migration)
# This should trigger UpdateLpsConfig() which pauses tasks and re-discovers addresses
message 'TC10b: Changing LPS address (triggers pause/resume)'
exec bash get-app-ip.sh local-manager
source .env

# Update LPS address with a port change (same IP, different representation)
# This triggers the code path with pause() in UpdateLpsConfig()
eden controller edge-node update --device local_profile_server=$app_ip:8888

# Wait for EVE to process the LPS address change
exec sleep 15

# Update the LPS config with new boot order
exec -t 2m bash set-vm-boot-order.sh $vm_uuid nousb
exec -t 2m bash wait-vm-config-applied.sh

# Verify appbootinfo shows LPS as source with NOUSB boot order after address change
exec -t 3m bash verify-appbootinfo.sh $vm_uuid BOOT_ORDER_NOUSB BOOT_ORDER_SOURCE_LPS

# Verify EVE received the new config after LPS address change
message 'TC10c: Verify config received after LPS address change'
exec -t 2m bash verify-eve-received-config-v2.sh $vm_uuid nousb
stdout 'EVE received boot order config'

# Restart VM to apply and verify
eden pod stop {{template "test_vm"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 20m HALTED {{template "test_vm"}}
eden pod start {{template "test_vm"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 10m RUNNING {{template "test_vm"}}

exec bash record-timestamp.sh

# Step 3: Verify config persisted - check fw_cfg is still nousb
message 'TC10d: Verify fw_cfg=nousb persisted after EVE reboot'
exec -t 2m bash verify-hypervisor-config-v2.sh $vm_uuid nousb
stdout 'fw_cfg USB boot: nousb'

# Step 4: Verify VM boots from HDD (proves nousb config was restored from disk)
# If config didn't persist, VM would boot from USB (Debian) since no resolution is set
message 'TC10e: Verify VM boots from HDD (Ubuntu) after EVE reboot'
exec -t 2m bash verify-boot-os-v2.sh {{template "test_vm"}} ubuntu
stdout 'BOOT OS VERIFIED'

# Cleanup
eden pod delete {{template "test_vm"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 5m - {{template "test_vm"}}

# Clear device property
eden controller edge-node update --config app.boot.order=

message '=== TC10 PASSED ==='

# ============================================================================
# TC11-13: HTTP Status Code Tests
# Tests: 200/201 (OK), 204 (No Content), 404 (Not Found/Throttle)
# ============================================================================
message '=== TC11-13: Testing HTTP status codes ==='

# Clean LPS state before test
exec -t 1m bash clean-lps-state.sh

# Ensure VM is deployed
eden pod delete {{template "test_vm"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 5m - {{template "test_vm"}}
eden pod deploy -n {{template "test_vm"}} --memory=1024MB --vnc-display=1 --fml -p {{template "vm_port"}}:22 --adapters $usb_adapter https://cloud-images.ubuntu.com/releases/focal/release-20210510/ubuntu-20.04-server-cloudimg-amd64.img --networks={{template "network"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 10m RUNNING {{template "test_vm"}}

exec bash get-vm-uuid.sh {{template "test_vm"}}
source .env

# --- TC11: HTTP 200/201 - Normal config response ---
message 'TC11: Testing HTTP 200/201 (normal config response)'
exec -t 2m bash set-vm-boot-order.sh $vm_uuid usb
exec -t 2m bash wait-vm-config-applied.sh

# Verify appbootinfo shows LPS as source with USB boot order
exec -t 3m bash verify-appbootinfo.sh $vm_uuid BOOT_ORDER_USB BOOT_ORDER_SOURCE_LPS

# Verify EVE received the config (200/201 response)
exec -t 2m bash verify-eve-received-config-v2.sh $vm_uuid usb
stdout 'EVE received boot order config'

# Verify EVE is polling at normal interval (not throttled)
exec -t 1m bash verify-polling-interval.sh normal
stdout 'Polling interval: normal'

message 'TC11 PASSED: 200/201 response handled correctly'

# --- TC12: HTTP 204 - No Content (no config changes) ---
# LPS returns 204 when the config file ModTime hasn't changed since last request.
# This tests that EVE preserves existing boot order when receiving 204.
message 'TC12: Testing HTTP 204 (no content - config unchanged)'

# Set initial config to usb, wait for EVE to fetch it
exec -t 2m bash set-vm-boot-order.sh $vm_uuid usb
exec -t 2m bash wait-vm-config-applied.sh

# Verify appbootinfo shows LPS as source with USB boot order
exec -t 3m bash verify-appbootinfo.sh $vm_uuid BOOT_ORDER_USB BOOT_ORDER_SOURCE_LPS

# Verify EVE received the initial config
exec -t 2m bash verify-eve-received-config-v2.sh $vm_uuid usb
stdout 'EVE received boot order config'

# Wait for EVE to poll again - LPS will return 204 since file wasn't modified
# (no touch, no content change)
message 'TC12a: Waiting for 204 response (no file modification)'
exec sleep 15

# Verify boot order is still applied correctly after 204
eden pod stop {{template "test_vm"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 20m HALTED {{template "test_vm"}}
eden pod start {{template "test_vm"}}
exec -t 5m bash wait-for-running-once.sh {{template "test_vm"}}

exec bash record-timestamp.sh

message 'TC12b: Verify fw_cfg=usb preserved after 204 responses'
exec -t 2m bash verify-hypervisor-config-v2.sh $vm_uuid usb
stdout 'fw_cfg USB boot: usb'

message 'TC12c: Verify VM still boots from USB (Debian) - config preserved'
exec -t 2m bash verify-boot-os-v2.sh {{template "test_vm"}} debian
stdout 'BOOT OS VERIFIED'

exec -t 1m bash verify-polling-interval.sh normal
stdout 'Polling interval: normal'

message 'TC12d: Testing HTTP 200 with same content (should behave like 204)'

# Touch the file to update ModTime - LPS will return 200 with same content
exec -t 1m bash touch-lps-config.sh

# Wait for EVE to poll and receive 200 with same content
exec sleep 15

# Verify boot order is still applied correctly (EVE detected no change)
eden pod stop {{template "test_vm"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 20m HALTED {{template "test_vm"}}
eden pod start {{template "test_vm"}}
exec -t 5m bash wait-for-running-once.sh {{template "test_vm"}}

exec bash record-timestamp.sh

message 'TC12e: Verify fw_cfg=usb preserved after 200 with same content'
exec -t 2m bash verify-hypervisor-config-v2.sh $vm_uuid usb
stdout 'fw_cfg USB boot: usb'

message 'TC12f: Verify VM still boots from USB (Debian)'
exec -t 2m bash verify-boot-os-v2.sh {{template "test_vm"}} debian
stdout 'BOOT OS VERIFIED'

message 'TC12 PASSED: 204 and 200-with-same-content preserve boot order'

# --- TC13: HTTP 404 - Not Found (triggers throttling) ---
message 'TC13: Testing HTTP 404 (not found - triggers throttle)'

# Remove the config file to trigger 404 response
exec -t 2m bash trigger-lps-404.sh

# Wait for EVE to POST and receive 404
exec sleep 70

# Verify EVE switched to throttled polling (1 hour interval)
exec -t 1m bash verify-polling-interval.sh throttled
stdout 'Polling interval: throttled'

# Restore config file and verify EVE recovers
message 'TC13a: Verify recovery from 404 throttle'
exec -t 2m bash set-vm-boot-order.sh $vm_uuid nousb

# Need to wait for throttle period or trigger immediate fetch
# The TriggerAppBootInfoPOST is called when LPS config changes
eden controller edge-node update --device local_profile_server=$app_ip:8888
exec -t 2m bash wait-vm-config-applied.sh

# Verify appbootinfo shows LPS as source with NOUSB boot order after recovery
exec -t 3m bash verify-appbootinfo.sh $vm_uuid BOOT_ORDER_NOUSB BOOT_ORDER_SOURCE_LPS

# Verify EVE received config and is back to normal polling
exec -t 2m bash verify-eve-received-config-v2.sh $vm_uuid nousb
stdout 'EVE received boot order config'

exec -t 1m bash verify-polling-interval.sh normal

# PHASE 3: EVE REBOOT PERSISTENCE TESTS (Most Complex)

# ============================================================================
# TC17: Persistence - Verify boot config persists across EVE reboot
# This tests that saveAppBootConfig/loadSavedAppBootConfig work correctly
#
# We use nousb with NO custom resolution to properly test:
# - Without nousb and without resolution: VM would boot from USB (Debian) by default
# - With nousb: VM boots from HDD (Ubuntu) regardless of resolution
# - After reboot: nousb should persist, so VM still boots from HDD (Ubuntu)
#
# NOTE: Requires TPM to be DISABLED in Eden config (eve.tpm = false) to avoid
# vcomlink startup issues after reboot.
# ============================================================================
message '=== TC17: Config persists across EVE reboot ==='

# Clean LPS state before test
exec -t 1m bash clean-lps-state.sh

# Explicitly clear custom resolution so OVMF would default to USB boot
# This makes the nousb setting the only thing preventing USB boot
eden controller edge-node update --config app.fml.resolution=

test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 5m - {{template "test_vm"}}

test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 5m - {{template "test_vm_2"}}

# Deploy fresh VM for reboot test WITH Controller boot_order=usb
# This allows testing LPS override (nousb) AND fallback to Controller (usb) after LPS clear
